headline: Corporate Coalition Commits $33M to Save the Colorado River
meta_description: Amazon and corporate partners launch $33M water conservation effort for stressed Colorado River Basin serving 40 million people across seven states.
summary_short: Amazon leads corporate push to conserve water in the Colorado River Basin with $33M committed to leak repairs, irrigation efficiency, and groundwater projects.
body:
Amazon has announced a $20 million investment to help restore the Colorado River, joining what may become the largest corporate water conservation effort focused on a single U.S. watershed. The e-commerce giant is launching the Colorado River Basin Collaborative alongside the Water Resilience Coalition and The Climate Pledge, aiming to fund irrigation improvements, leak detection, and groundwater recharge across the stressed basin. The effort has already secured more than $33 million in corporate commitments, with a goal of eventually raising $100 million. The Colorado River supplies water to nearly 40 million people and more than 5 million acres of farmland across seven U.S. states and Mexico—but 25 years of drought have reduced its annual flow by 20%, and its two largest reservoirs now sit below 30% capacity.

The initiative targets specific, tangible problems. Amazon is committing $2.2 million over three years to work with the Municipal Water District of Orange County, which serves 3.2 million residents, expanding leak detection and repair programs to communities that lack the resources to conduct this work independently. A second project partners with Arable, an agricultural technology company, to improve irrigation efficiency on tribal farmland in the Lower Colorado River Basin using sensors powered by Amazon Web Services—technology that gives farmers real-time data on crop water needs, significantly reducing draws from Lake Mead.

While federal policy sets the larger course—the Interior Department recently approved a management plan requiring the Lower Basin states of Nevada, California, and Arizona to reduce their annual Colorado River water deliveries by 1.25 million acre-feet over the next two years—corporate funding fills crucial gaps. These projects address how water is lost through agricultural delivery systems and aging urban infrastructure, working alongside government action to stabilize one of North America's most vital watersheds.
quick_facts: Amazon commits $20 million to Colorado River Basin water conservation
Corporate coalition has secured $33 million, targeting $100 million goal
Colorado River supplies 40 million people across 7 U.S. states and Mexico
$2.2 million project with Orange County serves 3.2 million residents
25 years of drought reduced river flow by 20 percent
